description:
WHAT IT IS MADE OF. Every token is a single loose heap of translucent quadrilaterals -- mostly squares and near-squares, rotated at varied angles -- stacked on a near-black, very slightly warm charcoal ground. A few soft-edged circles/discs are mixed in on some seeds. Everything is drawn with heavy alpha, so the picture is built almost entirely out of overlap: where two or three plates cross you get a darker or lighter tonal step, and the edges of the stack fade into the ground. There are only two colour families: a cool blue-grey slate and a warm amber/ochre. No line work, no texture, no type, no gradient other than what alpha stacking produces.

WHAT IT IS A PICTURE OF. It reads to me as a pile of translucent cards, slides or sheets of tinted glass dropped on a dark table and photographed from directly above -- or, on the denser seeds, as a plaque: one big amber backing plate with a dark slate slab laid across it. The central slab is not a plain rectangle; on several seeds (9369, and the 512 single) it is a jagged, notched, torn-edged polygon repeated three or four times at slightly different rotations and offsets around one centre, which gives it a stamped/echoed look, like a rough die-cut shape printed several times slightly out of register. Around that centre a scatter of smaller squares drifts outward like debris or sparks from the pile.

WHAT THE TWELVE HAVE IN COMMON. Identical ground, identical two-colour palette, identical vocabulary (rotated translucent quads + occasional disc), identical construction logic (a dense centre, a radial scatter, alpha overlap doing all the shading), and identical framing: the mass floats near the middle of a square frame with generous dark margin on all sides. Nothing bleeds off the edge; 9369 comes closest to the top-right corner and still stops short.

HOW THEY DIFFER. Chiefly in three things: overall scale of the heap, density, and how much amber is present. At one end 9369 and 10622 are large and dominated by a single big warm plate that occupies maybe 40-45% of the frame, with a clear figure/ground reading (dark slab on amber field). In the middle, 9011, 9548, 9727, 10085, 10264 and 10801 are medium heaps where slate and amber interleave and no single element dominates. At the other end 9190, 10443 and 10980 are sparse confetti -- a dozen small squares scattered widely with only a small amber pip near the centre, no dominant form at all, and a great deal of empty ground. 9906 is the outlier for colour: it is essentially all grey, with no visible amber at all, and it carries a large soft dark disc at its centre. Discs appear on 9190, 9906, 10085, 10264 and 10801 and are absent elsewhere.

WHAT HAPPENS ACROSS THE THREE STATES (seeds 9011, 9190, 9369, 9548). Neutral is the most consolidated and the coolest: the plates sit tightly on top of one another, amber is present but suppressed under the slate. Stress does three things at once and does them consistently on all four seeds -- the heap DISPERSES (elements separate, drift further from centre, the silhouette becomes looser and gappier), the amber gets both LARGER and BRIGHTER (9548 stress grows a big saturated ochre plate at upper right that is not there in neutral; 9369 stress rotates its amber plate and pushes it down-left so a whole warm corner is exposed; 9190 stress gains a bright amber square at centre-right), and DISCS APPEAR or grow (9011 stress gains two grey discs upper-left and right that neutral does not have; 9369 stress gains two prominent dark discs sitting on the amber). Recovery goes back most of the way toward neutral but not all of it: it is re-consolidated and re-stacked, but retains slightly more warmth and slightly more disc presence than neutral (9369 recovery keeps a large pale amber field, 9548 recovery keeps a small dark disc at centre, 9011 recovery is very nearly neutral again with a marginally looser stack). So the arc reads as: tight and cool -> scattered, hot and pocked -> re-gathered, faintly scarred.

WHAT SURVIVES AT 120px. The silhouette and the density class survive well. At browse size you can still separate the big-plate seeds (9369, 10622, and to a lesser degree 9548, 10264, 10085) from the medium heaps (9011, 9727, 10801) from the sparse scatters (9190, 10443, 10980) -- the twelve do not collapse into one repeated stamp. The amber accent is the single most legible feature at that size and it does most of the identifying work. What does NOT survive is fine incident: the jagged notching of the central slab flattens into a plain blob, the small satellite squares on 10443 and 10980 dim almost into the ground (10443 at 120px is close to invisible -- a faint smudge of dark grey on dark grey), and the internal tonal steps from overlap largely merge. The state change is still visible at 120px on 9369, 9548 and 9190, where the amber grows and moves; on 9011 the neutral/stress/recovery difference at 120px is subtle and I would call it marginal rather than obvious.

THINGS THAT LOOK LIKE MISTAKES. In 10622 there is a hard near-black rectangle at lower left that reads as a punched hole rather than a plate. A handful of tiny dark specks sit on the amber in 10622 and 10443 and read as dust rather than as elements. 9548 neutral has a thin bright amber sliver at the top of the stack that reads as a stray remnant of a plate hidden behind the others. On the sparse seeds the outermost squares are so isolated and so close in value to the ground that they read as leftovers rather than as composition.
